name: jimtcl
why: A tiny embeddable Tcl with a small footprint, an unusual language implementation that's easy to try in minutes.

brief.what_it_is: Jim is a small-footprint implementation of the Tcl programming language, written from scratch. It runs ordinary Tcl scripts and can also be embedded in a larger C application so that the application can be scripted in Tcl. The README says it covers many Tcl 8.5 and 8.6 features (such as {*}, dict, lassign and tailcall) and omits some, including traces and Tk. The Homebrew package installs a jimsh shell, a jimdb debugger and a build-jim-ext helper, but the README does not describe those tools.
brief.why_it_exists: The author started it in January 2005 as a way to "vent my need to hack on Tcl", and the README pitches it for scripting applications without linking a large system and for embedded systems. The stated goal is to keep Tcl's familiar syntax and tooling in a footprint small enough to ship inside a program.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the core is about 14k lines of C and that a build with default extensions at -Os is about 130k, or about 85k with no extensions. Extensions are loaded dynamically and some are pure Tcl, which keeps the base interpreter small. Values are dual-ported objects, so the string form and the internal form can both be used without repeated conversion.

Lists the optional extensions that can be enabled at build time.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps beyond building from source with ./configure and make. It names no accounts, runtimes or hardware. The brew formula is the only install path I saw, and I did not verify the executables it installs.
brief.standout: It is a full Tcl dialect in a tiny C interpreter, not a new little language, and it puts scripting inside the program so the script version ships with the app. The README also says the interpreter has its own GC for lambdas and references, and that arrays act as sugar over dicts.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README is the GitHub msteveb/jimtcl page. Its only date is the 10 Mar 2005 history note, and I did not check release tags or recent commits.
brief.caveats: The official homepage https://jim.tcl.tk/index.html did not load, so this brief rests on the GitHub README alone. The README says traces and Tk are not implemented and probably never will be. It reports speed as faster than Tcl 7.6p2 and slower than Tcl 8.4. It says tests exist, and it lists tested platforms as Linux, FreeBSD, MacOSX, eCos, QNX and Windows XP (mingw, MVC). The README does not give a licence name; it gives a BSD-style notice with copyright lines for many contributors.
quotes: A small-footprint implementation of the Tcl programming language.
Jim is not the next "little language", but it's a Tcl implementation.
Jim is simple with 14k lines of core code. If you want to adapt it you can hack the source code to meet the needs of your application.
